schema: candidate campus footprints. a package is a way of getting to 500+ contiguous buildable acres — by combining what is already on record, by targeting ground that fits the screen, or by taking someone else's assembled site.

types.combine: Built from sites already on record
types.target: Constructed from the screen — ground to go and get, not yet found

packages.name: Redding pair
packages.thesis: The only two tracts in the whole file sitting in the same small town. If they touch, or are separated only by a section-line road, this is the largest single footprint available without finding anything new.
packages.blockers: Both are cut by watercourses — the larger one carries two rivers and only 530 tillable acres of 1,232. Ringgold scores 47 and is bracketed by Clarke, which is closed, and Taylor, which is drafting.
packages.next: Ask the two listing brokers whether the parcels adjoin. Nick Hopp holds one and Jared Luebbers the other, so it is two calls.

packages.name: Davis County pair
packages.contiguous: no — Bloomfield and Floris are separate localities
packages.thesis: Two tracts over 500 acres in one county, which normally means one trip and one board to persuade.
packages.blockers: Davis has the worst assemblage profile on the screen at 7.4 owners per section, and the ground is recreational — ponds, timber and a cabin on one, unresolved flood extent on the other. These cannot merge into a single campus.
packages.next: Low priority. Keep as a fallback rather than working it.

packages.name: Buena Vista county position
packages.thesis: Two independent shots in a county scoring 78 with 3.4 owners per section and no ordinance action. One is a full off-market section with willing owners; the other is a clean 775-acre auction tract. Same county, same regional council, same board — the entitlement work is shared even though the sites are not.
packages.blockers: These are two campuses, not one. Section 16 carries Zone A across much of its area with no Base Flood Elevation. The auction tract runs on someone else's clock.
packages.next: Establish the dry, contiguous acreage inside Section 16. That single answer decides whether this county position is worth building around.

packages.name: Kossuth section
packages.thesis: The deepest pool of large holdings in Iowa — 396 farms at 500+ acres and 143 above 1,000, at a median of 228 acres. Roughly three signatures for a full section. Nothing on record here, and two loaded contacts already cover it.
packages.blockers: Nothing identified yet. This is a package to go and build, not one to evaluate.
packages.next: Mid Iowa Growth Partnership covers Kossuth and has not been called. NIACOG covers it too.

packages.name: Cherokee section
packages.thesis: The easiest assemblage arithmetic in the state at 2.7 owners per section, on Northwest Iowa Plains — the best landform class Iowa has. Well drained, gently rolling, sparse streams.
packages.blockers: Adjacent to two counties that have already closed, so the political weather could change. Smaller pool than Kossuth at 204 farms above 500 acres.
packages.next: Siouxland Interstate Metropolitan Planning Council covers Cherokee and Ida. One call reaches both.

packages.name: Mills Crossings Mega Site
packages.thesis: Larger than anything else in the project and the diligence is already paid for. State certification means Phase I environmental, geotechnical, archaeological and cultural review, utility verification and zoning confirmation are complete before a prospect looks. Minutes from I-29 and I-80 via US-34.
packages.blockers: Not contacted. Loess Hills and Missouri alluvial terrain in that part of the state needs checking site by site — flat ground there tends to be floodplain.
packages.next: Iowa Economic Development Authority holds the certified-site register. One email.

packages.name: Big Cedar Industrial Center
packages.thesis: Alliant Energy assembled 1,391 acres specifically to attract large load, and QTS has already taken 612 of it. Industrial zoning, rail and a counterparty whose business model is the project.
packages.blockers: Linn County's 18-month moratorium runs from 1 July 2026, but it applies to unincorporated county territory — the park sits inside Cedar Rapids city limits, so the city may be unaffected. Confirm which jurisdiction governs before spending time. Remaining capacity after QTS is unknown.
packages.next: Alliant Energy economic development. Ask what acreage remains and which jurisdiction has authority.

packages.name: Iowa Farmland — unqualified 2,700+ acres
packages.thesis: The largest acreage figure anywhere in the project. If it is one block it dwarfs everything else on record.
packages.blockers: No location, no parcel count, no owner, and contact was made through a website form rather than a conversation. It is equally likely to be a portfolio total across scattered listings.
packages.next: Phone them. One call establishes whether this is a single block or a spreadsheet total.
